title: LiteOdyssey: A Lightweight Reasoning AI Agent for Interpretable Rare-Disease Diagnosis
summary: Most medical AI systems improve by scaling additional machinery: more fine-tuning data, more agents, and/or larger retrieval databases. In rare-disease diagnosis, however, such scaling can produce systems that are difficult to deploy, audit, and maintain. We asked whether state-of-the-art diagnostic performance could instead be achieved by extending the reasoning chain of a single AI agent: guiding it with a diagnostic policy, developed through human-AI collaboration and augmenting with freely available biomedical tools. We introduce LiteOdyssey, a lightweight rare-disease diagnostic framework that guides reasoning language model through a clinical genetics workflow. This framework was developed through Policy Iteration with Human Feedback (PIHF) and uses dynamic access to public biomedical tools. On two challenging benchmarks that provide only patient clinical features, LiteOdyssey achieved state-of-the-art performance, with an overall disease Recall@1 of 59.3% over the combined 1,243 cases of LIRICAL (n = 370) and the PhenoPacket Store (n = 873). Both benchmarks have a high proportion of ultra-rare disease (a prevalence below 1 in 1,000,000, with ultra-rare shares of approximately 45% and 52.8%, respectively). On the more difficult PhenoPacket subset, where causal diseases were not mapped to Orphanet in our rarity-mapping pipeline, LiteOdyssey achieved 60.7% Recall@1, compared with 10.7% for the same baseline model (GPT-5.4) without tools. This performance was achieved without fine-tuning, multi-agent ensembles, or a large case-retrieval database. Gains were also observed in the following: on cases never seen during development, on a private cohort of real-world rare disease patients, and on a smaller open-weights model. LiteOdyssey suggests a path toward rare-disease AI systems that are accurate, easier to deploy, and more transparent for physician review.
tldr: LiteOdyssey is a lightweight, interpretable AI agent for rare-disease diagnosis that achieves state-of-the-art performance by extending a single reasoning language model's chain with a clinical genetics workflow and dynamic biomedical tool access, developed via human-AI policy iteration, without requiring fine-tuning or multi-agent ensembles.
tldr_zh: LiteOdyssey 是一个轻量级、可解释的罕见病诊断AI智能体，通过扩展单个推理语言模型的推理链，结合临床遗传学工作流程和动态生物医学工具访问，并采用人类-AI策略迭代开发，在无需微调或多智能体集成的情况下达到了最先进的性能。
summary_zh: 大多数医学人工智能系统通过扩展额外机制来提升性能：更多微调数据、更多代理和/或更大的检索数据库。然而，在罕见病诊断中，这种扩展可能导致系统难以部署、审计和维护。我们探究了是否可以通过延长单一人工智能代理的推理链来实现最先进的诊断性能：通过人机协作开发诊断策略来引导该代理，并利用免费可用的生物医学工具进行增强。我们引入了LiteOdyssey，这是一个轻量级的罕见病诊断框架，通过临床遗传学工作流程引导推理语言模型。该框架通过人类反馈策略迭代（PIHF）开发，并动态访问公共生物医学工具。在两个仅提供患者临床特征且具有挑战性的基准测试中，LiteOdyssey达到了最先进的性能，在LIRICAL（n=370）和PhenoPacket Store（n=873）的共计1,243例病例上，总体疾病Recall@1达到59.3%。这两个基准测试中超罕见疾病（患病率低于百万分之一，超罕见比例分别约为45%和52.8%）占比很高。在难度更大的PhenoPacket子集上（其中因果疾病在我们的罕见性映射流程中未映射到Orphanet），LiteOdyssey实现了60.7%的Recall@1，而未使用工具的相同基线模型（GPT-5.4）仅为10.7%。这一性能的达成无需微调、多代理集成或大型病例检索数据库。在以下方面同样观察到性能提升：在开发过程中从未见过的病例上、在真实世界罕见病患者的私人队列中、以及在较小的开源权重模型上。LiteOdyssey为构建准确、易于部署且更便于医生审查的罕见病人工智能系统指明了一条路径。

title: Attention-Based Prototype Calibration for Multi-Rater Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Few-shot medical image segmentation methods typically assume a single ground-truth annotation, overlooking systematic variability across expert raters commonly observed in clinical datasets. We propose an attention-based prototype calibration framework for few-shot multi-rater segmentation that models rater-specific deviations from a consensus representation in prototype space. A lightweight yet principled attention operator directly refines rater prototypes without modifying the backbone feature extractor, making the approach fully compatible with existing prototype-based few-shot segmentation methods. This design preserves semantic consistency while enabling personalized segmentation outputs with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on multi-rater medical imaging datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over baseline prototype approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of structured prototype calibration for modeling annotation variability. Our code is available at https://github.com/truong2710-cyber/JAPC.
tldr: The paper proposes an attention-based prototype calibration framework for few-shot medical image segmentation that models rater-specific deviations from a consensus prototype, enabling personalized segmentation with minimal computational overhead and compatibility with existing prototype-based methods.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种基于注意力的原型校准框架，用于少样本医学图像分割，该框架建模了不同标注者相对于共识原型的偏差，在最小计算开销下实现个性化分割输出，并与现有基于原型的少样本方法兼容。
summary_zh: 少样本医学图像分割方法通常假设单一真实标注，忽略了临床数据集中常见的不同专家评分者之间的系统性差异。我们提出了一种基于注意力的原型校准框架，用于少样本多评分者分割，该框架在原型空间中建模评分者特定偏差与共识表征之间的关系。一种轻量级且原理性的注意力算子直接优化评分者原型，无需修改主干特征提取器，使得该方法与现有的基于原型的少样本分割方法完全兼容。该设计在保持语义一致性的同时，以最小的计算开销实现个性化分割输出。在多评分者医学影像数据集上的实验表明，该方法相对于基线原型方法持续改进，突出了结构化原型校准在建模标注变异性方面的有效性。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/truong2710-cyber/JAPC 获取。

title: Propagating Structural Guidance: Synthesizing Fluorescein Angiography from Fundus Images and Sparse OCT Scans
summary: Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) is critical for assessing retinal vascular abnormalities, but its acquisition is invasive and not always feasible. In contrast, color fundus photography (CFP) is non-invasive and widely accessible, which has motivated studies on CFP-to-FFA synthesis. However, prior works rely solely on CFP surface texture, fundamentally limiting the ability to reconstruct functional vascular information and subtle pathological changes. To address this, we propose a novel framework that synthesizes FFA from CFP with structural guidance provided by optical coherence tomography (OCT). We construct a multi-modal retinal imaging dataset with paired CFP, FFA, and OCT from 3,676 patient eyes--the first tri-modally aligned dataset in retinal imaging. To bridge the spatial gap between OCT and fundus modalities, we propose a Spatially Aligned Cross-Modal Fusion (SACMF) module that projects depth-resolved OCT features onto the fundus plane and injects them into the CFP encoder via adaptive layer normalization. Beyond feature fusion, we further introduce Token-wise Cross-Modality Alignment (TCMA), a token-level contrastive learning strategy that explicitly aligns CFP and FFA representations at corresponding spatial positions. Our method achieves superior synthesis performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, extensive experiments demonstrate that the FFA images synthesized by our approach bring greater improvements in downstream disease diagnosis performance than existing methods, highlighting the clinical potential of our approach as a non-invasive decision-support tool in routine workflows. The code is available at https://github.com/while-plus/OCT-guide-FFA-Syn.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel framework to synthesize fluorescein angiography (FFA) from color fundus photography (CFP) using structural guidance from optical coherence tomography (OCT), introducing a spatially aligned cross-modal fusion module and token-wise cross-modality alignment for improved synthesis and downstream disease diagnosis.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种新颖框架，利用光学相干断层扫描（OCT）的结构引导，从彩色眼底摄影（CFP）合成荧光素血管造影（FFA），引入了空间对齐跨模态融合模块和令牌级跨模态对齐，以提高合成质量和下游疾病诊断性能。
summary_zh: 眼底荧光血管造影（FFA）对于评估视网膜血管异常至关重要，但其获取具有侵入性且并非总是可行。相比之下，彩色眼底摄影（CFP）无创且广泛可用，这推动了从CFP到FFA合成的研究。然而，先前的工作仅依赖CFP的表面纹理，从根本上限制了重建功能性血管信息和细微病理变化的能力。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种新颖框架，该框架利用光学相干断层扫描（OCT）提供的结构引导，从CFP合成FFA。我们构建了一个包含3,676只患者眼睛的配对CFP、FFA和OCT的多模态视网膜成像数据集——这是视网膜成像领域首个三模态对齐数据集。为弥合OCT与眼底模态之间的空间差异，我们提出了一种空间对齐跨模态融合（SACMF）模块，该模块将深度分辨的OCT特征投影到眼底平面上，并通过自适应层归一化将其注入CFP编码器。除特征融合外，我们还进一步引入了令牌级跨模态对齐（TCMA），这是一种令牌级对比学习策略，可在对应空间位置上显式地对齐CFP和FFA表示。与现有最先进方法相比，我们的方法实现了更优异的合成性能。此外，大量实验表明，与现有方法相比，我们方法合成的FFA图像在下游疾病诊断性能上带来了更大的改进，凸显了该方法作为常规工作流程中无创决策支持工具的临床潜力。代码可在 https://github.com/while-plus/OCT-guide-FFA-Syn 获取。
